## 3. User — 2026-08-16T18:02:22.717Z

Review target: `only review the change NO EDITING NO FIXING JUST REPORT`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

<result>Review complete. I read the full 22,797-line diff plus the working-tree source for hot-path modules (engine, ffmpeg_source, visualizer, ui, yt, main). No correctness issues on the agenda; findings below are efficiency-only. Line numbers are as of the working tree (the diff is a fresh-file staging, so they match).

## Efficiency findings

**1. `src/yt/mod.rs:75-79` — `resolve()` spawns yt-dlp twice, sequentially, per track start**
- **Summary**: `resolve()` = `video_meta()` (full `yt-dlp -J --no-playlist` run + parse of a ~600 KB JSON dump) followed by `yt_stream()` (a second `yt-dlp -g -f …` run) for the same video.
- **Cost**: Every track start (`Engine::build_stream`), every seek-recovery, and every watchdog EOF-drop rebuild pays two process spawns + two network round trips back-to-back on the *blocking worker thread* — roughly doubles per-track startup latency (1–4 s → 2–8 s) and is the dominant startup cost. The huge `-J` dump is parsed and then discarded except for 5 small fields.
- **Cheaper**: one `yt-dlp -J` invocation carrying the same `--extractor-args youtube:player_client=android` the `-g` leg uses plus the `-f` string, and read the direct URL from `formats` in the same dump. Halves spawns, round trips, and parses — one JSON parse per track instead of two. (The doc comment even notes the two legs differ only by that extractor arg.)

**2. `src/ui/visualizer.rs:48-100` — per-frame allocation storm at ~30 fps during playback**
- **Summary**: `render_visualizer` allocates `vec![0.0f32; w]`, clones it twice for smoothing (`src = cols.clone()`), then builds a fresh `Vec&lt;Span&gt;` per row with `ch.to_string()` per cell — up to 14 rows × 80 cols ≈ 1,100 styled `String`+`Span` allocs every frame while the spectrum is on screen.
- **Cost**: roughly 30–60k small allocations/second during any playback, on the render thread, on top of ratatui's own per-cell diffing. This is the hottest per-frame allocator in the diff.
- **Cheaper**: reuse persistent scratch buffers (the `FrameOut` struct already lives across frames — it can own `cols`), precompute the per-row color once per layout (color changes only with `vfrac`), and render columns from a static char table with a single `Style` per row rather than one `Span`/`String` per cell.

**3. `src/engine/ffmpeg_source.rs:132-150` — per-chunk conversion allocates twice and re-passes the chunk**
- **Summary**: `fold()` converts each 16 KB pump chunk into an intermediate `Vec&lt;i16&gt;` allocation, then `feed_interleaved` re-extends the visualizer's `VecDeque` (which grows past its `FFT_SIZE*2 = 2048` capacity every chunk, reallocating + memcpy), then `pending.extend` re-passes the samples to f32.
- **Cost**: ~3 allocations + 2 extra passes over 8,192 samples per ~93 ms of audio — steady-state memory churn of a few hundred KB/s on the audio path, and the `VecDeque` oscillates/grows on every chunk for the track's whole duration.
- **Cheaper**: one pass converting `&amp;[u8]` → `f32` into a single reusable scratch `Vec&lt;f32&gt;` (owned by the source; only reallocated when a chunk is larger than the last), feeding the visualizer and the pending pool from that same buffer.

**4. `src/app/persist.rs:237` / `src/main.rs:643` — full session store serialized + fs-written on the UI thread every 24 s**
- **Summary**: `save_state()` clones the whole `Store` (liked/albums/artists/playlists + 100-entry history, all owned Strings), serde-serializes, and writes `state.json` inline inside the select loop's frame-tick arm.
- **Cost**: the TUI freezes (no frames rendered) for the duration of the write every `SYNC_EVERY` (24 s) and on quit; the store can be hundreds of KB with history + playlists.
- **Cheaper**: run it via `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (the loop already has a runtime), and serialize from `&amp;App`/`&amp;Store` instead of a full `.clone()` first.

**5. `src/ui/library.rs:133-200`, `src/ui/lyrics.rs:74-86`, `src/ui/queue.rs:37-48` — per-frame `truncate()` String allocations for every visible list row**
- **Summary**: each rendered frame calls `truncate(&amp;item.name, max)` (→ `collect::&lt;String&gt;`) for every visible row in the library, lyrics, and queue views (up to ~50–80 rows), plus `format!("{:&gt;2} ", …)` in queue and `format!("{before}▏{after}")` in the search header.
- **Cost**: dozens of String/format allocations per frame at the 16–33 ms draw cadence whenever the list is visible; the rendered text only changes when the data, selection, or width changes.
- **Cheaper**: truncate to a `&amp;str` slice (no allocation; only the ellipsis case needs one), and cache the per-row label/styles keyed on `(name, max)` or rebuild rows only when the underlying display triple changes.

**6. `src/ui/nowplaying.rs:121-165` — progress-bar labels computed twice and colored span vector rebuilt per frame**
- **Summary**: `render_now_strip` formats `fmt_ms(pos)`/`fmt_ms(dur)` to size the hit rect, then `render_progress` formats them again, and both call `gradient_progress`, which allocates a `Vec&lt;Rgb&gt;` of full bar width + one `Span` per bar cell every frame.
- **Cost**: bar-width × ~2 `String`/`Span` allocations plus a second label formatting pass per redraw — small, but it is per-frame on the always-visible bottom strip at up to 33 ms cadence.
- **Cheaper**: compute `left`/`right` labels once and pass them down (or return the reserve from `render_now_strip`), and sample the gradient only at the `filled` boundary — the filled segment's colors step only when `filled` changes; cache `colors` across frames.

**7. `src/lyrics/fetch.rs:21-37` — a fresh `reqwest::blocking::Client` built per track change**
- **Summary**: `fetch_lyrics_blocking` constructs a whole new blocking client (connection pool, TLS stack init) on every metadata landing — the engine already keeps one long-lived shared client for the identical cover-fetch pattern.
- **Cost**: one client construction + connection teardown per track (fires on `spawn_blocking`, so no UI freeze, but it is pure repeated setup for a one-off GET).
- **Cheaper**: module-level `OnceLock&lt;reqwest::blocking::Client&gt;` (same pattern the engine uses with its `http_client()`).

**8. `src/ui/visualizer.rs:10-14, 44-48` — `bands` mutex taken twice per frame**
- **Summary**: `render_visualizer` does `try_lock()` for the `is_active` check, then again to read `values`/`peak_envelope`; `run_ui` also `try_lock`s `bands` every 16 ms tick for the `animating` flag.
- **Cost**: three mutex acquisitions per frame where one would do. Trivial, but it is in the hottest path; the UI could read `(is_active, values, peak)` in one lock and the animating check could reuse the previous frame's result.

## Checked and clean

- No closure-held large scopes: every long-lived closure (engine error callback, `souvlaki` attach, watchdog, `resume_source` spawn, meta-thread) captures only small handles or `Arc`s; the meta thread takes a bounded clone of `ResolvedTrack`.
- Config is `OnceLock`d (read once); `yt_json`/`spawn_ffmpeg` don't re-read files.
- The TUI frame gating (`should_draw`/`ArtRepaint`) already avoids most wasted redraws; cover re-encode is correctly cached by area.
- The 100 ms worker tick, the 5 s watchdog, `Engine::queue()` snapshot clone, and the FFT core (band ranges + hann window precomputed; `VisBands` reads via `try_lock` so the audio thread never blocks) are all appropriately bounded.

Most valuable first: the double yt-dlp invocation (#1) roughly halves startup latency per track and every recovery; #2 and #3 are steady per-frame/per-chunk allocation churn in the two performance-critical loops.</result>

### Commit 7 — (#8) `save_state` off the UI thread

**Files**: `src/main.rs`, `src/app/persist.rs`.

**Changes**:
- Change `SaveState::save` usage: we cannot move `SaveState` into a `blocking` task directly (it is `serde`-de `'static`-friendly), so the helper becomes:
  ```rust
  pub(crate) fn save_state_async(app: &amp;App) {  // inside run_ui loop
      let app = app.clone(); // App: Clone? App is NOT Clone (grep verified no derive)
  ```
  — App is **not** Clone, so the plan is: extract a value struct `Snapshot` (files `src/main.rs`) that is built synchronously from `&amp;App` and is `serde::Serialize + Send`. The serialization+write moves to `spawn_blocking(move || snapshot.persist())`. The snapshot is cheap: clone strings, clone vectors (store clone is the costly part and stays on the blocking side).
  Actually the cheapest correct shape: split `save_state(&amp;app)` into
  - `fn snapshot_session(app: &amp;App) -&gt; Snapshot` (pure clone of the ~8 fields + `store.clone()`);
  - `impl Snapshot { fn persist(&amp;self) }` — renamed from the current `SavedState::save` body, which does `serde_json::to_string` + optional `create_dir_all` + non-atomic `fs::write`.
  - In `run_ui`: `let snap = snapshot_session(&amp;app); tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || snap.persist());` at the three call sites (:642, :656, :663). For the quit paths, the task must **complete before exit**: replace `save_state(&amp;app)` before `break` with `runtime.block_on`? — we are inside an async fn, so use `let handle = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(...); let _ = handle.await;` (shorter: `handle.await.ok();`). The sync-every tick does not need await — fire-and-forget is fine for the periodic save.
  - **Keep** the non-atomic write behavior? Current `fs::write` is non-atomic (persist.rs:220–228) — keep semantics identical (this commit is only about the thread), so `persist` keeps `create_dir_all` + `fs::write`. Atomicity is a separate issue, not in scope (#20 could make it atomic, but that is a behavior change beyond cache_dir re-routing — flag as optional).
- `SavedState::load` unchanged.

**Invariant**: a crash mid-save may not lose more than the same window as today (the sync-every window is 24s either way); quit always persists.

Add `gradient::sample_into(stops, n, out: &amp;mut [Rgb])` (and make `sample` call it with `Vec::with_capacity`); add `Rgb` indexing into the progress spans. Replace `gradient_progress(width, filled, stops, track)` with a variant that takes `colors: &amp;[Rgb]` (the caller's scratch). The volume meter (:189–200) has `Vec&lt;Span&gt;` per bar and `ch.to_string()` per bar — its VLEV array is 8 chars, per-frame cost is 8×`to_string` — adopt the same `&amp;[Rgb]`-based builder for the 8 bars: `gradient_progress` already returns a Vec&lt;Span&gt;; use `components::progress_spans(colors, filled, track)` producing the track-colored tail. This also fixes the bug I found: `render_volume`'s click region width is hard-coded `13` (:213) while the meter emits `8 bars + " NNN%"` = 12 cells — the code and the hit rect disagree by one cell; unify by having the meter return its content width.
- Latex/emoji none.

**Invariant**: `truncate` output bytes are identical to today — the UB-warning-free Cow version keeps the two quirks and never splits a multibyte char (the "…" splice is appended after `s.chars().take(...)`); all tests/util.rs truncate cases updated to `&amp;*` form pass with identical output. `render_progress`/hit-rect width math must produce the same bar rect as today except the corrected volume rect (13→12).

### Commit 12 — (#3) radio policy constants one home

**Files**: `src/yt/mod.rs`, `src/engine/expander.rs`, `src/engine/mod.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/input/key.rs`, `src/ui/nowplaying.rs` (no).

**Changes**:
- **Design decision (validated)**: because `yt` already imports `crate::engine::RADIO_LIMIT`, moving the constants into `yt` would create a dependency inversion **only if** `engine` imported them back. The deliverable says "keep domain ownership in yt"; with engine importing `yt::RADIO_LIMIT` the loop is `engine → yt → crate::engine` (compile-time const provenance — legal but morally inverted). Since `RADIO_LIMIT` is **already** re-exported by `engine` for its public API (`pub use expander::{... RADIO_LIMIT}` engine/mod.rs:32), the honest fix is: define `expander::RADIO_LIMIT` (already there), re-export through engine (already there), and make **yt** read `crate::engine::expander::RADIO_LIMIT` directly — i.e., no new home in yt, just **delete the two `const _: () = assert!` pins** (yt/mod.rs:95–96) and the invented arithmetic block (`RADIO_FETCH_LIMIT` becomes `crate::engine::RADIO_LIMIT.min(40)` — the `if`/`else` collapses). Remove the `RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS` from main.rs and put it in `src/yt/mod.rs` as `RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS`, with main.rs and key.rs importing `tuna_tui::yt::RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS`. The one-liner rationale: the deadline and the fetch cap are both YouTube real-estate policies; they belong with the yt code, while the station cap stays in the engine's expander. This flips the `main → engine` const import into `main → yt`.
- `yt/mod.rs:87–96` block replaced by `const RADIO_FETCH_LIMIT: usize = crate::engine::RADIO_LIMIT.min(40);` — **no assertion needed** since `.min` is safe at runtime; the two asserts go away.
- main.rs:441 constant moves to yt; `RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS` usages (main.rs:804, key.rs:217) become `yt::RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS` (or `tuna_tui::yt::RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS`).

## Section 4 — Per-commit gate script

For each commit (1–20), from a **clean checkout at the previous commit**:
```bash
set -euo pipefail
cargo fmt --all --check                                   # never touches the tree
RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
cargo test --all-features
# txc-only gate for commits touching lib-common code (#19, #20, and any yt/config change):
cargo check --no-default-features --features txc
# engine-behavior commits (#5, #10, #12, #16, #17 → source commits 2,3,13,14,20):
cargo test --all-features -- --ignored live_radio_roundtrip live_resolve_roundtrip live_album_drill_in_roundtrip live_playlist_drill_in_roundtrip   # needs network + yt-dlp
cargo build --example probe                                 # engine-api commits (examples/probe compiles)
# Optional per-commit release sanity:
git stash &amp;&amp; cargo build --release &amp;&amp; git stash pop         # never before committing
```
CI itself runs fmt/clippy/test on {ubuntu, macos, windows}; the plan keeps every commit within those.

bugs are being hunted; these are quality fixes only. Git policy: **local commits only,
no push**; tracked as **20 beads (bd)**, created up-front, closed as each commit lands.

154	pub(crate) fn fetch_detail_blocking(
155	    store: &Store,
156	    uri: &str,
157	    name: &str,
158	) -> (String, Vec<LibItem>) {
159	    // "Play all" row first.
160	    let mut items = vec![LibItem::play(format!("▶︎ Play {name}"), uri.to_string())];
161	
162	    let (_, kind, id) = match uri_parts(uri) {
163	        Some(p) => p,
164	        None => return (name.to_string(), items),
165	    };
166	
167	    match kind {
168	        // A playlist whose contents have grown locally renders its own rows;
169	        // otherwise the network copy (flat-extracted) is the contents.
170	        "playlist" if store.playlist_tracks(uri).is_some() => {
171	            let rows = store.playlist_tracks(uri).expect("checked above");
172	            items.extend(
173	                rows.iter()
174	                    .map(|t| LibItem::track(t.name.clone(), t.subtitle.clone(), t.uri.clone())),
175	            );
176	            if items.len() == 1 {
177	                items.push(LibItem::header("empty playlist"));
178	            }
179	        }
180	        "playlist" => {
181	            let before = items.len();
182	            items.extend(playlist_rows(&format!(
183	                "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list={id}"
184	            )));
185	            if items.len() == before {
186	                items.push(LibItem::header("no tracks — empty or restricted"));
187	            }
188	        }
189	        "channel" => {
190	            let before = items.len();
191	            items.extend(playlist_rows(&format!(
192	                "https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}/videos"
193	            )));
194	            if items.len() == before {
195	                items.push(LibItem::header("no uploads — empty or restricted"));
196	            }
197	        }
198	        "album" => {
199	            // YouTube has no first-class albums; the saved slug searches.
200	            let before = items.len();
201	            items.extend(
202	                yt::search(id, config::get().search_limit)
203	                    .into_iter()
204	                    .map(|v| LibItem::track(v.title, v.artist, v.uri)),
205	            );
206	            if items.len() == before {
207	                items.push(LibItem::header("nothing loaded — search failed"));
208	            }
209	        }
210	        "video" => {
211	            if let Some(v) = yt::video_meta(id) {
212	                items.push(LibItem::track(v.title, v.artist, v.uri));
213	            } else {
214	                items.push(LibItem::header("couldn't load — check the network"));
215	            }
216	        }
217	        _ => {}
218	    }
219	
220	    (name.to_string(), items)
221	}

223	/// The rows of a playlist / mix / channel-tab dump. Flat entries are
224	/// title-only — split "Artist - Title (…)" so the list isn't long pasted
225	/// strings.
226	fn playlist_rows(url: &str) -> Vec<LibItem> {
227	    yt::playlist_entries(url)
228	        .into_iter()
229	        .map(|v| {
230	            let (name, subtitle) = title_artist_split(&v.title);
231	            LibItem::track(name, subtitle, v.uri)
232	        })
233	        .collect()
234	}
235	
236	/// Split a YouTube title at a power-separator: "Artist - Title (Official
237	/// Video)" → ("Title (Official Video)", "Artist"). Falls back to the whole
238	/// string (subtitle empty) when no separator exists.
239	fn title_artist_split(s: &str) -> (String, String) {
240	    for sep in [" – ", " - ", " — ", "-"] {
241	        if let Some((artist, title)) = s.split_once(sep) {
242	            return (title.trim().to_string(), artist.trim().to_string());
243	        }
244	    }
245	    (s.to_string(), String::new())
246	}

/// Extend `items` with `rows`; when the source yielded nothing (an empty or
/// restricted playlist, a failed search), push a header `hint` instead.
/// Returns whether rows were added.
fn append_or_hint(
    items: &mut Vec<LibItem>,
    rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = LibItem>,
    hint: &str,
) -> bool {
    let before = items.len();
    items.extend(rows);
    if items.len() == before {
        items.push(LibItem::header(hint));
        false
    } else {
        true
    }
}

/// The history rows shared by Home's Recently Played / Top Tracks and the
/// Recent section: one mapping so `PlayedEntry`'s shape stays in sync
/// everywhere.

    rows: impl Iterator<Item = &'a PlayedEntry> + 'a,
) -> impl Iterator<Item = LibItem> + 'a {

}

+/// Extend `items` with `rows`; when the source yielded nothing (an empty or
+/// restricted playlist, a failed search), push a header `hint` instead.
+/// Returns whether rows were added.
+fn append_or_hint(
+    items: &mut Vec<LibItem>,
+    rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = LibItem>,
+    hint: &str,
+) -> bool {
+    let before = items.len();
+    items.extend(rows);
+    if items.len() == before {
+        items.push(LibItem::header(hint));
+        false
+    } else {
+        true
+    }
+}
+
+/// The history rows shared by Home's Recently Played / Top Tracks and the
+/// Recent section — one mapping so `PlayedEntry`'s shape stays in sync
+/// everywhere it renders.
+fn history_rows<'a>(
+    rows: impl Iterator<Item = &'a PlayedEntry> + 'a,
+) -> impl Iterator<Item = LibItem> + 'a {
+    rows.map(|h| LibItem::track(h.title.clone(), h.artist.clone(), h.uri.clone()))
+}
+
 /// The rows of a playlist / mix / channel-tab dump. Flat entries are
 /// title-only — split "Artist - Title (…)" so the list isn't long pasted
 /// strings.

1	//! On-disk cache for catalogue reads (`~/.cache/tuna-tui/api`).
2	//!
3	//! Spotify's development-mode quota is per app, and it runs out: an artist
4	//! drill-in costs four requests, so a few minutes of browsing can earn a `429`
5	//! with a `Retry-After` measured in hours. Cached bodies keep repeat visits off
6	//! the network entirely, and a stale entry is served when the request fails —
7	//! an album list from yesterday beats an empty page.
8	//!
9	//! Only immutable-ish catalogue data belongs here. Anything the user can change
10	//! (playback state, saved-track flags) must go straight to the API.
11	
12	use std::fs;
13	use std::hash::{DefaultHasher, Hash, Hasher};
14	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
15	use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
16	use std::sync::OnceLock;
17	use std::time::Duration;
18	
19	/// Entries older than this are swept once per run. Album art is the bulk of it
20	/// — a few hundred KB a day, which would otherwise just accumulate forever.
21	const KEEP: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30 * 24 * 60 * 60);
22	
23	/// Where a URL's cached body lives. The hash keeps tokens and query strings out
24	/// of the filename.
25	fn path_in(dir: &Path, url: &str) -> PathBuf {
26	    let mut h = DefaultHasher::new();
27	    url.hash(&mut h);
28	    dir.join(format!("{:016x}", h.finish()))
29	}
30	
31	fn dir() -> Option<&'static Path> {
32	    static DIR: OnceLock<Option<PathBuf>> = OnceLock::new();
33	    DIR.get_or_init(|| {
34	        let dir = crate::home_dir()?.join(".cache/tuna-tui/api");
35	        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).ok()?;
36	        #[cfg(unix)]
37	        {
38	            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
39	            let _ = fs::set_permissions(&dir, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700));
40	        }
41	        sweep(&dir, KEEP);
42	        Some(dir)
43	    })
44	    .as_deref()
45	}

/// flat-playlist equivalent of `api/library.rs`'s region-locked-row skip.
fn video_from(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<YtVideo> {
    let id = v["id"].as_str()?.to_string();
    let title = v["title"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let artist = v["artist"]
        .as_str()
        .or_else(|| v["channel"].as_str())
        .or_else(|| v["uploader"].as_str())
        .unwrap_or("")
        .to_string();
    let album = v["album"].as_str().map(String::from);
    let duration_ms = v["duration"]
        .as_u64()
        // checked_mul: `s * 1000` would wrap/panic on a hostile `-J` dump
        // (u64::MAX × 1000 overflows before the u32 try_from can guard it).
        .and_then(|s| s.checked_mul(1000))
        .and_then(|ms| u32::try_from(ms).ok());
    let thumbnail = largest_thumbnail(v);
    let uri = format!("yt:video:{id}");
    Some(YtVideo {
        id,
        uri,
        title,
        artist,
        album,
        duration_ms,
        thumbnail,
    })
}

/// The last thumbnail in the array — yt-dlp orders `thumbnails` small→large, so
/// the last is the biggest actual frame. Falls back to the bare `thumbnail`.
fn largest_thumbnail(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<String> {
    v["thumbnails"]
        .as_array()

    fn resolve(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<ResolvedTrack, String> {
        let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(uri) else {
            return Err(format!("not a track uri: {uri}"));
        };
        yt::resolve(&id)
            .map(ResolvedTrack::from)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("couldn't resolve {uri}"))
    }

    fn radio(&self, seed: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(seed) else {
            return Err(format!("not a track uri: {seed}"));
        };
        // `radio_entries` caps the mix fetch to one inner-page (a full RD mix
        // paginates 15+ API calls and blows past the app's radio deadline),
        // falls back across the mix id variants, and ends in a search-built
        // pseudo-radio when YouTube has no mix for the seed at all.
        let rows = yt::radio_entries(&id);
        station_from(seed, rows)
    }
}

/// The seed first, then the mix rows — the seed itself skipped when the mix
/// echoes it, the whole list capped to `RADIO_LIMIT` + 1. Pure (no network), so
/// the station-shape logic is unit-tested offline; only the mix fetch is live.
fn station_from(seed: &str, rows: Vec<yt::YtVideo>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let mut uris = vec![seed.to_string()];
    for row in rows.into_iter().take(RADIO_LIMIT) {
        if row.uri != seed {
            uris.push(row.uri);
        }
    }
    if uris.len() == 1 {
        return Err(format!("radio station for {seed} came back empty"));
    }
    Ok(uris)
}

fn entries_of(url: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let rows = yt::playlist_entries(url);
    if rows.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("{url} yielded no entries"));
    }
    Ok(rows.into_iter().map(|r| r.uri).collect())
}

            artist: s.video.artist,

/// Normalize a video id / `yt:video:` uri / watch URL to a watch URL. The
/// URL builders own the canonical youtube.com shapes, so every layer (the yt
/// resolver, the expander, browse) shares one spelling.
pub fn video_url(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if url_or_id.starts_with("http://") || url_or_id.starts_with("https://") {
        return Some(url_or_id.to_string());
    }
    if let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(url_or_id) {
        return Some(format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={id}"));
    }
    // A bare id — but only a bare one: a `yt:playlist:` or other non-video uri
    // must not masquerade as a video id.
    if url_or_id.contains(':') {
        return None;
    }
    (!url_or_id.is_empty()).then(|| format!("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={url_or_id}"))
}

/// The canonical playlist URL (`yt:playlist:<id>` → youtube.com).
pub fn playlist_uri(id: &str) -> String {

}

}

/// appending `/best` rather than letting resolution fail.
const STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT: &str = "android";

/// Run `yt-dlp … -g` and return the first printed line — the direct stream URL.
fn yt_stream(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let url = watch_url(url_or_id)?;
    let configured = config::get().audio_format.clone();
    // `bestaudio/best` under the android client means `best` (the muxed
    // stream) — but a user who set `bestaudio` without a fallback must not
    // hard-fail resolution, so always carry the `/best` tail.
    let format = if configured.contains('/') {
        configured
    } else {
        format!("{configured}/best")
    };
    yt_stdout(
        &["-g", "-f", &format],
        &[
            "--no-playlist",
            &url,
            "--extractor-args",
            &format!("youtube:player_client={STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT}"),

{
  "replace_all": false,

  "old_string": "/// Convert a `yt:kind:id` URI to its youtube.com equivalent. Other schemes\n/// (the synthetic `tuna:action:` rows) have no shareable URL and return \"\".\npub fn uri_to_url(uri: &str) -> String {\n    let Some((scheme, kind, id)) = uri_parts(uri) else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    match (scheme, kind) {\n        (\"yt\", \"video\") => format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={id}\"),\n        (\"yt\", \"playlist\") => format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list={id}\"),\n        (\"yt\", \"channel\") => format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}\"),\n        _ => String::new(),\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Convert a `yt:kind:id` URI to its youtube.com equivalent. Other schemes\n/// (the synthetic `tuna:action:` rows) have no shareable URL and return \"\".\n/// The video/playlist shapes delegate to the single-owner builders below;\n/// the channel card (`/channel/{id}`) stays distinct from the uploads tab\n/// ([`channel_videos_url`]) that drill-ins expand.\npub fn uri_to_url(uri: &str) -> String {\n    let Some((scheme, kind, id)) = uri_parts(uri) else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    match (scheme, kind) {\n        (\"yt\", \"video\") => video_url(uri).unwrap_or_default(),\n        (\"yt\", \"playlist\") => playlist_uri(id),\n        (\"yt\", \"channel\") => format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}\"),\n        _ => String::new(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Normalize a video id / `yt:video:` uri / watch URL to a watch URL. These\n/// builders own the canonical youtube.com shapes, so every layer (the yt\n/// resolver, the expander, browse) shares one spelling.\npub fn video_url(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if url_or_id.starts_with(\"http://\") || url_or_id.starts_with(\"https://\") {\n        return Some(url_or_id.to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(id) = track_id_from_uri(url_or_id) {\n        return Some(format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={id}\"));\n    }\n    // A bare id — but only a bare one: a `yt:playlist:` or other non-video uri\n    // must not masquerade as a video id.\n    if url_or_id.contains(':') {\n        return None;\n    }\n    (!url_or_id.is_empty()).then(|| format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={url_or_id}\"))\n}\n\n/// The canonical playlist URL.\npub fn playlist_uri(id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list={id}\")\n}\n\n/// The canonical channel uploads tab — what a `yt:channel:` drill-in expands.\npub fn channel_videos_url(id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"https://www.youtube.com/channel/{id}/videos\")\n}"
}

/// How long a radio request may take before the app gives up. The station
/// fetch is capped to one inner-page (~4s), so this only covers the rare
/// fallback chain (mix-id variants + a search-built station) and genuine
/// network stalls — 12s was shorter than an un-capped mix's pagination alone

/// How many entries the radio fetch asks for — the engine's station cap,

/// Kick off one radio fetch: the seed is resolved on a blocking thread with a
/// deadline, and the result (or the timeout error) lands on `chans.radio`.
/// The in-flight guard + status text are the caller's job.
fn spawn_radio(
    engine: Engine,
    seed: String,
    start_position_ms: u32,
    tx: flume::Sender<Result<Radio, String>>,
) {
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        let res = match tokio::time::timeout(
            Duration::from_secs(tuna_tui::yt::RADIO_TIMEOUT_SECS),
            async move {
                tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || engine.radio_tracks(&seed))
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
            },
        )
        .await
        {
            Ok(r) => r.map_err(|e| e.to_string()),
            Err(_) => Err("timed out (radio endpoint unresponsive)".to_string()),
        };
        let _ = tx.send(res.map(|uris| Radio {
            uris,
            start_position_ms,
        }));
    });
}
```

pub fn resolve_kind(kind: &str, id: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<YtVideo>, String> {

        "channel" => entries_of_url(&channel_videos_url(id)),

}

```rust

pub(crate) fn render_progress(f: &mut Frame, app: &App, theme: Theme, area: Rect) {
    let (pos, dur) = match &app.playback.now {
        Some(n) => (app.playback.position_ms(), n.duration_ms.max(1)),
        None => (0, 1),
    };
    // Compute the bar width from the exact label lengths so the duration sits
    // flush against the right edge (aligned with the volume meter above it).
    let left = format!("{} ", fmt_ms(pos));
    let right = format!(" {}", fmt_ms(dur));
    let reserve = left.chars().count() + right.chars().count();
    let bar_w = (area.width as usize).saturating_sub(reserve);
    let filled = ((pos as f32 / dur as f32) * bar_w as f32) as usize;

    let mut spans = vec![Span::styled(left, theme.muted())];
    spans.extend(gradient_progress(
        bar_w,
        filled,
        &[theme.primary, theme.accent],
        theme.border_dimmest,
    ));
    spans.push(Span::styled(right, theme.muted()));
    f.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Line::from(spans)), area);

/// Fill `out` with `n` gradient samples (reusing the caller's buffer).
pub fn sample_into(stops: &[Rgb], n: usize, out: &mut Vec<Rgb>) {

    out.reserve(n);
    for i in 0..n { out.push(stops-sample(i, n)); }  // need the same math as sample
}
pub fn sample(stops: &[Rgb], n: usize) -> Vec<Rgb> {

}

//! The Lyrics view.

use crate::*;

pub(crate) fn render_lyrics(f: &mut Frame, app: &App, theme: Theme, area: Rect) {
    let inner = area.inner(Margin::new(2, 0));
    if inner.height == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let max = inner.width as usize;

    // Header: current track title + "artist · album", above the lyrics.
    let mut lyrics_area = inner;
    if let Some(n) = app.playback.now.as_ref() {
        let head = Layout::vertical([
            Constraint::Length(1), // title
            Constraint::Length(1), // artist / album
            Constraint::Length(1), // spacer
            Constraint::Min(1),    // lyrics
        ])

92	    let path = path_in(dir, url);
93	    if let Some(max_age) = max_age {
94	        let age = fs::metadata(&path)
95	            .and_then(|m| m.modified())
96	            .ok()?
97	            .elapsed()
98	            .ok()?;
99	        if age > max_age {
100	            return None;
101	        }
102	    }
103	    fs::read_to_string(&path).ok()
104	}
105	
106	fn put_in(dir: &Path, url: &str, body: &str) {
107	    write_atomic(&path_in(dir, url), body.as_bytes());
108	}
109	
110	/// Album art, keyed the same way. Spotify's image URLs embed a content hash, so
111	/// a cached file never goes stale — the URL changes when the picture does.
112	pub fn get_bytes(url: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
113	    fs::read(path_in(dir()?, url)).ok()
114	}
115	
116	pub fn put_bytes(url: &str, bytes: &[u8]) {
117	    if let Some(dir) = dir() {
118	        write_atomic(&path_in(dir, url), bytes);
119	    }
120	}
121	
122	/// Write via a temporary file and rename, so a kill mid-write can't leave a
123	/// truncated entry behind — image bytes never expire, and a corrupt one would
124	/// mean a cover that stays broken forever.
125	///
126	/// The temp name carries a counter because two library threads can fetch the
127	/// same URL at once; sharing one scratch file would interleave their writes into
128	/// a corrupt entry that then never expires.
129	fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) {
130	    static SEQ: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
131	    let tmp = path.with_extension(format!("{}.tmp", SEQ.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));
132	    if fs::write(&tmp, bytes).is_ok() && fs::rename(&tmp, path).is_err() {
133	        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
134	    }
135	}

3	use crate::*;

5	/// Mouse hit rects, written by the renderer and read only by `handle_mouse`.
6	///
7	/// Output only: nothing here is threaded frame-to-frame, and every rect is
8	/// (re)set or cleared on the frame that draws the thing it belongs to. The one
9	/// exception is `scroll_len`, which is written with `scroll` but not cleared
10	/// alongside it — reading it is only sound because `handle_mouse` checks
11	/// `scroll` is `Some` first.
12	#[derive(Default)]
13	pub(crate) struct HitRects {
14	    /// Last-rendered progress-bar rect (for click-to-seek).
15	    pub(crate) bar: Option<Rect>,
16	    /// Last-rendered sidebar scrollbar track + item count (drag-to-scroll).
17	    pub(crate) scroll: Option<Rect>,
18	    pub(crate) scroll_len: usize,

25	}

28	/// can take `&App`.

30	pub(crate) struct FrameOut {
31	    pub(crate) hits: HitRects,
32	    /// Library viewport start row. Unlike `hits`, this is read-modify-write:
33	    /// the renderer feeds the previous frame's value into `scroll_offset` and
34	    /// stores the result back, which is what makes scrolling sticky. Owned by
35	    /// `run_ui` so it survives across frames.
36	    pub(crate) lib_offset: usize,
37	}

39	/// What the album art box owes the next frame.
40	///
41	/// `ratatui-image` puts the whole image in one cell's symbol and marks the rest
42	/// of the box `Skip`, which the diff never touches again — so leftovers stay,
43	/// and a re-encode is byte-identical for sixel and iTerm2 and gets discarded.
44	/// Blanking the box for one frame is the only change the diff will emit, and it
45	/// makes the image that follows one too.
46	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
47	pub(crate) enum ArtRepaint {
48	    /// The box holds what it should.
49	    Idle,
50	    /// Blank the box this frame.
51	    Wipe,
52	    /// Draw the art; the wipe has gone out.
53	    Draw,
54	}
55	
56	impl ArtRepaint {
57	    pub(crate) fn advance(self) -> Self {
58	        match self {
59	            Self::Wipe => Self::Draw,
60	            _ => Self::Idle,
61	        }
62	    }
63	}

66	pub(crate) const MIN_FRAME: Duration = Duration::from_millis(16);
67	/// Redraw rate while the visualizer or a theme fade is running.
68	pub(crate) const ANIM_FRAME: Duration = Duration::from_millis(33);
69	/// Redraw rate when nothing changed — enough to keep the clock and progress bar
70	/// honest without repainting an identical frame 60 times a second.
71	pub(crate) const IDLE_REDRAW: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
72	/// How often the live queue is re-fetched and the session persisted.
73	pub(crate) const SYNC_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(24);
74

76	///
77	/// Input beats animation beats the idle clock. Smoothness of the recolour comes
78	/// from its duration, not from the frame rate: every present makes the terminal
79	/// recompose the viewport, and the inline cover shimmers if that happens 60
80	/// times a second.
81	pub(crate) fn should_draw(dirty: bool, animating: bool, since_last: Duration) -> bool {
82	    if dirty {
83	        since_last >= MIN_FRAME
84	    } else if animating {

1	//! The spectrum bars drawn under the album art.
2	
3	use crate::*;
4	
5	pub(crate) fn render_visualizer(f: &mut Frame, app: &App, theme: Theme, area: Rect) {
6	    let active = app
7	        .svc
8	        .engine
9	        .bands
10	        .try_lock()
11	        .map(|g| g.is_active)
12	        .unwrap_or(false);
13	    if !active {
14	        return;
15	    }
16	    let Ok(guard) = app.svc.engine.bands.try_lock() else {
17	        return;
18	    };
19	    let values: [f32; NUM_BANDS] = guard.values;
20	    let peak = guard.peak_envelope.max(1e-6);
21	    drop(guard);
22	
23	    // Cap the spectrum to a centered band — full-pane bars are too tall/wide.
24	    let vh = ((area.height as u32 * 3 / 5) as u16)
25	        .clamp(6, 14)
26	        .min(area.height);
27	    let vw = ((area.width as u32 * 9 / 10) as u16)
28	        .clamp(24, 80)
29	        .min(area.width);
30	    let vrect = Rect {
31	        x: area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(vw) / 2,
32	        y: area.y + area.height.saturating_sub(vh) / 2,
33	        width: vw,
34	        height: vh,
35	    };
36	    let w = vrect.width as usize;
37	    let h = vrect.height as usize;
38	    if w == 0 || h == 0 {
39	        return;
40	    }
41	
42	    // 1. Box-average the bands into each column (anti-aliasing vs. single-pick).
43	    let mut cols = vec![0.0f32; w];
44	    for (x, c) in cols.iter_mut().enumerate() {
45	        let lo = x * NUM_BANDS / w;
46	        let hi = (((x + 1) * NUM_BANDS / w).max(lo + 1)).min(NUM_BANDS);
47	        let sum: f32 = values[lo..hi].iter().sum();
48	        let v = sum / (hi - lo) as f32;
49	        // Perceptual curve so quiet detail stays visible.
50	        *c = (v / peak).sqrt().clamp(0.0, 1.0);
51	    }
52	
53	    // 2. Spatial smoothing — a couple of weighted passes so the envelope flows
54	    //    instead of spiking. This is what kills the "chopped" look.

/// `focused` → `border_active`; otherwise `border_subtle`.
pub fn left_bar_block(theme: &Theme, focused: bool, bg: Color) -> Block<'static> {
    let bar_color: Color = if focused {
        theme.border_active.into()
    } else {
        theme.border_subtle.into()
    };
    Block::default()
        .borders(Borders::LEFT)
        .border_type(BorderType::Thick)
        .border_style(Style::default().fg(bar_color))
        .style(Style::default().bg(bg))
}

/// A gradient horizontal progress/segment bar as a span vector.
///
/// `width` cells total; `filled` cells (0..=width) use the gradient, the rest use
/// the theme's dimmest border color as a track. Uses a solid block glyph so it
/// reads clean at any width.
pub fn gradient_progress<'a>(
    width: usize,
    filled: usize,
    stops: &[Rgb],
    track: Rgb,
) -> Vec<Span<'a>> {
    let filled = filled.min(width);
    let colors = gradient::sample(stops, width.max(1));
    (0..width)
        .map(|i| {
            if i < filled {
                Span::styled("▬", Style::default().fg(colors[i].into()))
            } else {
                Span::styled("▬", Style::default().fg(track.into()))
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

Handy for coloring `n`\n/// visualizer bars or an `n`-cell progress bar in one shot.\npub fn sample(stops: &[Rgb], n: usize) -> Vec<Rgb> {\n    if n == 0 {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n    if n == 1 {\n        return vec![interpolate(stops, 0.0)];\n    }\n    (0..n)\n        .map(|i| interpolate(stops, i as f32 / (n - 1) as f32))\n        .collect()\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Sample `n` evenly-spaced colors across a gradient. Handy for coloring `n`\n/// visualizer bars or an `n`-cell progress bar in one shot.\n///\n/// Falls back to [`sample_into`] with a fresh buffer; per-frame callers (the\n/// progress bar) reuse one via [`sample_into`] to skip the allocation.\npub fn sample(stops: &[Rgb], n: usize) -> Vec<Rgb> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n    sample_into(stops, n, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Like [`sample`], but appends to the caller's buffer (cleared + reused).\npub fn sample_into(stops: &[Rgb], n: usize, out: &mut Vec<Rgb>) {\n    out.clear();\n    if n == 0 {\n        return;\n    }\n    if n == 1 {\n        out.push(interpolate(stops, 0.0));\n        return;\n    }\n    out.extend((0..n).map(|i| interpolate(stops, i as f32 / (n - 1) as f32)));\n}"
}

  "old_string": "/// A gradient horizontal progress/segment bar as a span vector.\n///\n/// `width` cells total; `filled` cells (0..=width) use the gradient, the rest use\n/// the theme's dimmest border color as a track. Uses a solid block glyph so it\n/// reads clean at any width.\npub fn gradient_progress<'a>(\n    width: usize,\n    filled: usize,\n    stops: &[Rgb],\n    track: Rgb,\n) -> Vec<Span<'a>> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(width);\n    let mut colors = Vec::with_capacity(width);\n    gradient_progress_into(width, filled, stops, track, &mut colors, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Like [`gradient_progress`], but fills caller-owned buffers (cleared + reused)\n/// — the per-frame steady state, where the renderer keeps a scratch `Vec` for\n/// the gradient colors and one for the spans.\npub fn gradient_progress_into<'a>(\n    width: usize,\n    filled: usize,\n    stops: &[Rgb],\n    track: Rgb,\n    colors: &mut Vec<Rgb>,\n    out: &mut Vec<Span<'a>>,\n) {\n    out.clear();\n    if width == 0 {\n        return;\n    }\n    let filled = filled.min(width);\n    let track_style = Style::default().fg(track.into());\n    gradient::sample_into(stops, width, colors);\n    for (i, &color) in colors.iter().enumerate() {\n        let style = if i < filled {\n            Style::default().fg(color.into())\n        } else {\n            track_style\n        };\n        out.push(Span::styled(\"▬\", style));\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// A gradient horizontal progress/segment bar as a span vector.\n///\n/// `width` cells total; `filled` cells (0..=width) use the gradient, the rest use\n/// the theme's dimmest border color as a track. Uses a solid block glyph so it\n/// reads clean at any width.\npub fn gradient_progress<'a>(\n    width: usize,\n    filled: usize,\n    stops: &[Rgb],\n    track: Rgb,\n) -> Vec<Span<'a>> {\n    let filled = filled.min(width);\n    let colors = gradient::sample(stops, width.max(1));\n    (0..width)\n        .map(|i| {\n            if i < filled {\n                Span::styled(\"▬\", Style::default().fg(colors[i].into()))\n            } else {\n                Span::styled(\"▬\", Style::default().fg(track.into()))\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}"
}

  "new_string": "pub(crate) fn render_progress(\n    f: &mut Frame,\n    app: &App,\n    out: &mut FrameOut,\n    theme: Theme,\n    area: Rect,\n    left: String,\n    right: String,\n) {\n    let (pos, dur) = match &app.playback.now {\n        Some(n) => (app.playback.position_ms(), n.duration_ms.max(1)),\n        None => (0, 1),\n    };\n    let reserve = left.chars().count() + right.chars().count();\n    let bar_w = (area.width as usize).saturating_sub(reserve);\n    let filled = ((pos as f32 / dur as f32) * bar_w as f32) as usize;\n\n    // Direct cell writes — the bar is a single-char run with one color per\n    // cell (plus the two labels), so span/paragraph plumbing is pure overhead.\n    let buf = f.buffer_mut();\n    buf.set_stringn(area.x, area.y, &left, left.chars().count() as u16, theme.muted());\n    let colors = &mut out.scratch.bar_colors;\n    gradient::sample_into(&[theme.primary, theme.accent], bar_w, colors);\n    for (i, &color) in colors.iter().enumerate() {\n        let fg = if i < filled {\n            color.into()\n        } else {\n            theme.border_dimmest.into()\n        };\n        let cell = buf.get_mut(area.x + reserve as u16 + i as u16, area.y);\n        cell.set_symbol(\"▬\");\n        cell.set_fg(fg);\n    }\n    let right_x = area.x + (reserve + bar_w) as u16;\n    buf.set_stringn(right_x, area.y, &right, right.chars().count() as u16, theme.muted());\n}"

1	//! A rodio `Source` that plays raw interleaved s16 PCM from an ffmpeg child's
2	//! stdout pipe.
3	//!
4	//! `ffmpeg -v error -ss <pos> -i <url> -f s16le -ac 2 -ar 44100 -` is spawned
5	//! by the engine; the child's stdout is handed to this source, which the audio
6	//! device's thread pulls through rodio's queue/player chain. Every read chunk
7	//! is tee'd into the shared [`Visualizer`] bands on the way past — the same
8	//! "tee'd sink" design the librespot backend used, minus librespot.
9	//!
10	//! # Why a pump thread
11	//!
12	//! The pipe is read by a *pump thread*, never by the audio callback. A
13	//! blocking `read()` in `next()` wedges cpal's callback thread the instant
14	//! ffmpeg's pipe is momentarily empty, and the device starts faulting
15	//! (`Buffer underrun/overrun` storm). The source instead drains a channel
16	//! without ever blocking; an empty channel (ffmpeg still starting, or jitter)
17	//! yields silence, so the device keeps streaming.
18	//!
19	//! A small prebuffer (≈93 ms) is filled before playback hands over the first
20	//! real sample, so ffmpeg's bursty start-up never reaches the listener as a
21	//! hole. Position authority stays the playhead: `frames` counts *stereo frames
22	//! actually popped* (converted from a chunk, not received) and position is
23	//! `start_ms + frames/44.1`.
24	//!
25	//! EOF is the pipe closing: the pump exits with `eof = true`, the source pops
26	//! the remaining buffer, then `Iterator::next` returns `None` and rodio's
27	//! queue fires the sound-done signal the engine awaits.
28	
29	use std::collections::VecDeque;
30	use std::io::Read;
31	use std::process::ChildStdout;
32	use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
33	use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
34	use std::time::Duration;
35	
36	use rodio::{ChannelCount, Sample, SampleRate, Source};
37	
38	use crate::audio::{VisBands, Visualizer};
39	
40	/// Bytes per pump read (16 KiB = 4096 stereo frames ≈ 93 ms).
41	const READ_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024;
42	/// Raw samples (floats) to accumulate before the first pop — the prebuffer.
43	/// 8 KiB of float samples = 4096 stereo frames ≈ 93 ms of latency.
44	const PREBUFFER_SAMPLES: usize = 8 * 1024;
45	
46	/// The rodio source for one ffmpeg child. Cheap to build; the expensive pipe
47	/// I/O happens on the pump thread started inside [`FfmpegSource::new`].
48	pub(crate) struct FfmpegSource {
49	    /// Converted chunks from the pump, in delivery order.
50	    pending: VecDeque<f32>,
51	    /// Stereo frames delivered so far (the playhead authority).
52	    frames: Arc<AtomicU64>,
53	    /// The FFT tee writing to the renderer's shared bands.
54	    visualizer: Visualizer,
55	    /// Set when the pump saw the pipe close. After the pending pool drains
56	    /// past this, `next()` reports EOF rather than playing silence forever.
57	    eof: bool,
58	    /// The engine kills this source by flipping the flag ahead of the child:
59	    /// `next()` then ends immediately instead of draining buffered PCM at
60	    /// device speed — a swapped/seeked-away track must not keep sounding.
61	    cancelled: Arc<AtomicBool>,
62	    /// Prebuffer is a start-up concern only: once the first real sample has
63	    /// been served, later delivery gaps play silence directly instead of
64	    /// re-gating and stalling the queue.
65	    started: bool,
66	    /// Live chunks from the pump thread. Bounded to ~8 reads (≈0.75 s of
67	    /// audio): the pump blocks on a full queue — on *its own* thread, never on
68	    /// the audio callback — instead of letting a burst decode flood memory.
69	    chunks: flume::Receiver<Vec<u8>>,
70	}
71	
72	impl FfmpegSource {
73	    /// Build the source over ffmpeg's stdout. `bands` is the shared cell the
74	    /// FFT tee writes into (the same `Arc` the renderer reads); `cancelled`
75	    /// is owned by the engine, which flips it to abort this source.
76	    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
77	    pub(crate) fn new(
78	        stdout: ChildStdout,
79	        frames: Arc<AtomicU64>,
80	        bands: Arc<Mutex<VisBands>>,
81	        cancelled: Arc<AtomicBool>,
82	    ) -> Self {
83	        let (tx, chunks) = flume::bounded(8);
84	        // The pump: blocking `read`s live here, never on cpal's callback
85	        // thread. It ends when the pipe closes (natural EOF or a killed
86	        // child), or when the source (and so `tx`) goes away.
87	        std::thread::Builder::new()
88	            .name("ffmpeg-pump".into())
89	            .spawn(move || {
90	                let mut stdout = stdout;
91	                let mut buf = [0u8; READ_BYTES];
92	                loop {
93	                    match stdout.read(&mut buf) {
94	                        Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
95	                        Ok(n) => {
96	                            if tx.send(buf[..n].to_vec()).is_err() {
97	                                break; // the source is gone
98	                            }
99	                        }
100	                    }
101	                }
102	                // The end-marker: read() itself never yields an empty chunk,
103	                // so an empty Vec is unambiguous. Without it the source would
104	                // play silence forever (eof never flips, the done-signal never
105	                // fires, the track never ends).
106	                let _ = tx.send(Vec::new());
107	            })
108	            .expect("spawn ffmpeg pump");
109	        Self {
110	            pending: VecDeque::with_capacity(PREBUFFER_SAMPLES),
111	            frames,
112	            visualizer: Visualizer::new(bands, 44_100.0),
113	            eof: false,
114	            cancelled,
115	            started: false,
116	            chunks,
117	        }
118	    }
119	
120	    /// Fold what the pump has delivered into `pending`, teeing into the
121	    /// visualizer, non-blocking. The empty end-marker flips `eof` (see the
122	    /// pump thread).
123	    ///
124	    /// The pull is *bounded*: `pending` is kept at prebuffer depth, never
125	    /// grown greedily. Draining the whole channel on every call let the pump
126	    /// outrun playback — instant for local files, bursty for network — hit
127	    /// EOF, and freeze the FFT tee while `pending` still held seconds of
128	    /// audio (the 2026-08-16 "visualizer moves, then stops as the music
129	    /// starts" bug). Pushing only when the pool is low keeps delivery paced
130	    /// to the playhead, so the tee stays fed for the whole track, and the
131	    /// channel's backpressure moves the pump block off the callback thread.
132	    fn fold(&mut self) {
133	        while self.pending.len() < PREBUFFER_SAMPLES {
134	            match self.chunks.try_recv() {
135	                Ok(chunk) if !chunk.is_empty() => {
136	                    let ints: Vec<i16> = chunk
137	                        .chunks_exact(2)
138	                        .map(|c| i16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
139	                        .collect();
140	                    self.visualizer.feed_interleaved(&ints);
141	                    self.pending
142	                        .extend(ints.iter().map(|&s| s as f32 * (1.0 / 32768.0)));
143	                }
144	                Ok(_) => {
145	                    // The empty end-marker: pipe closed, no more audio. It is
146	                    // only consumed once the pool dips below the target, which
147	                    // the drain always does — `eof_signals` still fires when
148	                    // the last buffered sample is popped.
149	                    self.eof = true;
150	                    break;
151	                }
152	                Err(_) => break, // nothing delivered yet — play silence this tick
153	            }
154	        }
155	    }
156	
157	    fn eof_signals(&self) -> bool {
158	        self.eof && self.chunks.is_empty()
159	    }
160	}
161	
162	impl Iterator for FfmpegSource {
163	    type Item = Sample;
164	
165	    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
166	        // Killed ahead of the child (track swapped/seeked away): end now.
167	        // Draining the buffered PCM at device speed would keep the old song
168	        // audible for the channel's whole backlog (~1.5 s after a busy tool).
169	        if self.cancelled.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
170	            return None;
171	        }
172	        self.fold();
173	        // Prebuffer: hold back real audio until there's ~93 ms of it, so the
174	        // device never tears on ffmpeg's start-up. Silence here is *not*
175	        // counted against the playhead — and the gate is startup-only, so a
176	        // delivery gap later in the track plays silence directly instead of
177	        // re-arming the stall.
178	        if !self.started {
179	            if self.pending.len() < PREBUFFER_SAMPLES && !self.eof {
180	                return Some(0.0);
181	            }
182	            self.started = true;
183	        }
184	        match self.pending.pop_front() {
185	            Some(s) => {
186	                // One float = one channel sample; every second pop completes
187	                // a stereo frame. Counted here — delivered to the device — so
188	                // a fast local decode can't race the playhead ahead of what
189	                // has actually reached the listener.
190	                if self.pending.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
191	                    self.frames.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
192	                }
193	                Some(s)
194	            }
195	            None if self.eof_signals() => None,
196	            // Channels raced ahead of fold (awaiting the pump) — play silence
197	            // rather than blinking the device.
198	            None => Some(0.0),
199	        }
200	    }
201	}
202	
203	impl Source for FfmpegSource {
204	    /// Raw PCM has no intrinsic span; `None` keeps the queue's span open until
205	    /// the iterator itself ends (pipe close).
206	    fn current_span_len(&self) -> Option<usize> {
207	        None
208	    }
209	
210	    fn channels(&self) -> ChannelCount {
211	        ChannelCount::new(2).expect("stereo")
212	    }
213	
214	    fn sample_rate(&self) -> SampleRate {
215	        SampleRate::new(44_100).expect("44.1 kHz")
216	    }
217	
218	    fn total_duration(&self) -> Option<Duration> {
219	        None
220	    }
221	}

```rust
/// The lib-toggle arms of run_action share one body; only the message pair
/// differs per store kind. (added, removed) — byte-identical to the old arms.
fn toggle_msg(kind: StoreKind) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
    match kind {
        StoreKind::Liked => ("added to Liked \u{2665} (press r to refresh)", "removed from Liked"),
        StoreKind::Artist => ("following", "unfollowed"),
        StoreKind::Album => ("saved album", "removed album"),
        StoreKind::Playlist => ("added to library", "removed from library"),
    }
}
```

Then a shared toggle helper:
```rust
/// Apply a store toggle and return its status message. `subtitle` blank for
/// kinds that have none (artists).
fn toggle_store(app: &mut App, kind: StoreKind, uri: String, name: String, subtitle: String) -> String {
    let (added, removed) = toggle_msg(kind);
    if app.store.toggle(kind, name, subtitle, uri) {
        added.into()
    } else {
        removed.into()
    }
}
```

And the four arms become `ActionKind::ToggleLike { uri, name, subtitle } => toggle_store(app, StoreKind::Liked, uri, name, subtitle),` etc. Queue/AddToPlaylist/other arms untouched.

/// The shared context tail — Play / Open-<label> / CopyLink — appended by the
/// channel, album, and playlist arms. The video arm's Queue/AddToPlaylist tail
/// stays separate: a single table can't produce both orders.
fn push_context_tail(items: &mut Vec<ActionItem>, uri: &str, name: &str, open_label: &str) {
    items.push(ActionItem { label: "▶︎  Play".into(), kind: ActionKind::Play { uri: uri.into(), name: name.into() } });
    items.push(ActionItem { label: open_label.into(), kind: ActionKind::Open { uri: uri.into(), name: name.into() } });
    items.push(ActionItem { label: "⧉  Copy Link".into(), kind: ActionKind::CopyLink { uri: uri.into() } });
}

/// Restart the decoder on `url` at whole-second `pos` — shared by
/// `build_stream` and `seek_now`. Returns Err when spawn fails; on Err the
/// caller decides recovery. Never touches `state.playing` (paused-seek stays
/// paused; recovery-rebuild keeps its saved state).
fn restart_stream(
    &mut self,
    url: &str,
    uri: &str,
    duration_ms: Option<u32>,
    pos: u32,
    play: bool,
) -> Result<()> {
    let pos = pos / 1000 * 1000;

    let frames = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
    let cancelled = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    let source = FfmpegSource::new(
        stdout, Arc::clone(&frames), Arc::clone(&self.bands), Arc::clone(&cancelled),

    let done = self.queue.append_with_signal(source);
    if play {

        url: url.to_string(),

        duration_ms,

        frames,
        cancelled,
    });

    self.set_health(play);
    self.set_active(play);
    self.last_correction = Instant::now();

}

Revised pick_url:
```rust
/// Pull the direct stream URL out of a `-J` info dump, mirroring what the
/// old `-g -f <configured>/best` leg returned:
/// 1. a formats[] entry whose format_id equals a bare `configured`
///    (e.g. a user's `audio_format = "251"`);
/// 2. otherwise the last *playable* formats entry (android client dumps
///    append storyboard entries — sb* with no codecs — after the real
///    stream, so the naive "last entry" would hand out a storyboard URL);
/// 3. finally the info dict's own top-level `url` (= the `-f` selection).
fn pick_url<'a>(root: &'a serde_json::Value, configured: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    let bare = !configured.contains('/');
    if let Some(entries) = root["formats"].as_array() {
        if bare {
            if let Some(f) = entries.iter().find(|f| f["format_id"].as_str() == Some(configured)) {
                if let Some(u) = f["url"].as_str() {
                    return Some(u);
                }
            }
        }
        for f in entries.iter().rev() {
            let cross = f["vcodec"].as_str().unwrap_or("none") != "none"
                || f["acodec"].as_str().unwrap_or("none") != "none";
            if cross && f["url"].as_str().is_some() {
                return f["url"].as_str();
            }
        }
    }
    root["url"].as_str().or_else(|| root["formats"]...never)
}
```

A stalled URL starves the engine's\n/// prebuffer → silent playback, ALSA underrun errors, frozen position and\n/// visualizer, and watchdog rebuild loops.\n///\n/// Trade-off: the android client exposes no audio-only itags — `-f bestaudio`\n/// hard-fails under it, so the `/best` fallback below always lands on the\n/// muxed (360p video + audio) stream, wasting bandwidth the engine never\n/// decodes. That cost is deliberate: an unthrottled stream is worth 3× the\n/// bytes; a user-set `audio_format` without a fallback is tolerated by\n/// appending `/best` rather than letting resolution fail.\nconst STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT: &str = \"android\";\n\n/// Pull the direct stream URL out of a `-J` info dump — the same pick the old\n/// `-g -f <configured>/best` leg made, now from the dump's own data:\n/// 1. a `formats[]` entry whose `format_id` equals a bare `configured` (a\n///    user's `audio_format = \"251\"` must select that exact itag);\n/// 2. otherwise the *last playable* entry — the android dump appends\n///    storyboard entries (`sb*`, both codecs \"none\") after the real stream,\n///    so the naive \"last entry\" would hand back a storyboard URL;\n/// 3. finally the info dict's own top-level `url` — which with `-f` active is\n///    exactly the format `-g` would have printed.\nfn pick_url<'a>(root: &'a serde_json::Value, configured: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    if let Some(entries) = root[\"formats\"].as_array() {\n        if !configured.contains('/') {\n            if let Some(f) = entries\n                .iter()\n                .find(|f| f[\"format_id\"].as_str() == Some(configured))\n                .and_then(|f| f[\"url\"].as_str())\n            {\n                return Some(f);\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(f) = entries.iter().rev().find(|f| {\n            let playable = f[\"vcodec\"].as_str().is_some_and(|v| v != \"none\")\n                || f[\"acodec\"].as_str().is_some_and(|a| a != \"none\");\n            playable && f[\"url\"].as_str().is_some()\n        }) {\n            return f[\"url\"].as_str();\n        }\n    }\n    root[\"url\"].as_str()\n}"

New resolve:
```rust
pub fn resolve(url_or_id: &str) -> Option<StreamInfo> {
    let url = crate::util::video_url(url_or_id)?;
    let configured = config::get().audio_format.clone();
    // `bestaudio/best` under the android client means `best` (the muxed
    // stream) — but a user who set `bestaudio` without a fallback must not
    // hard-fail resolution, so always carry the `/best` tail.
    let format = if configured.contains('/') {
        configured.clone()
    } else {
        format!("{configured}/best")
    };
    // One `-J` serves both legs: the android extractor-arg (the unthrottle
    // mitigation) and the `-f` policy live here, and the metadata for
    // playback comes from the same dump (video_from below).
    let root = yt_json(&[
        "--no-playlist",
        "-f",
        &format,
        &url,
        "--extractor-args",
        &format!("youtube:player_client={STREAM_PLAYER_CLIENT}"),
    ])?;
    let video = video_from(&root)?;
    let url = pick_url(&root, &configured)?;
    Some(StreamInfo {
        url: url.to_string(),
        video,
    })
}
```
Note: yt_json signature `fn yt_json(extra: &[&str]) -> Option<Value>` — takes base + extra; the -J base is inside yt_json ✓. Video_meta unchanged.

# The one, fully-wired binary. `required-features` states what was already
# true — `main.rs` is unconditionally wired to the streaming engine — so that
# a protocol-only build (`--no-default-features --features txc`) skips the bin
# instead of failing to compile it.
[[bin]]
name = "tuna-tui"
path = "src/main.rs"
required-features = ["streaming"]

# Dev tools, kept as examples (cargo run --example theme_demo / probe).
[[example]]
name = "theme_demo"
path = "examples/theme_demo.rs"

[[example]]
name = "txc_demo"
path = "examples/txc_demo.rs"
required-features = ["txc"]

[[example]]
name = "probe"
path = "examples/probe.rs"
required-features = ["streaming"]

[profile.release]
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true
panic = "abort"

# The profile that 'dist' will build with
[profile.dist]
inherits = "release"
lto = "thin"

# Debian packaging (audit H7): the binary links libasound2 (rodio/cpal ALSA)
# and libssl3 (reqwest native-tls), so the .deb must declare them or `dpkg -i`
# installs a binary that fails to start with missing shared libraries.
[package.metadata.deb]
depends = "libasound2, libssl3"
section = "sound"
priority = "optional"
assets = [
